treeshapesim

Simulate rooted, binary, ultrametric trees in which topological imbalance and the distribution of branching times are set by separate parameters.

  • Topology: Aldous’ (1996) beta-splitting model. beta = 0 gives Yule trees, lower values give more imbalanced trees and higher values more balanced ones.
  • Branching times: a pure-birth process in which each of the k lineages splits at rate k^c. c = 0 is Yule, c < 0 slows diversification towards the present (negative gamma; Pybus & Harvey, 2000) and c > 0 speeds it up.

The gamma statistic depends only on the internode intervals and the Colless index only on the topology, so beta mainly moves the Colless index and c mainly moves gamma.

Documentation: https://diogoprov.github.io/treeshapesim/

Installation 

install.packages("treeshapesim", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
# or
remotes::install_github("diogoprov/treeshapesim")

Example 

library(treeshapesim)
set.seed(1)
tr <- sim_tree_shape(100, beta = -1, c = -0.5)   # imbalanced, early splits
tree_shape(tr)                                    # gamma and normalized Colless

# trees near target values of gamma and Colless
cal <- calibrate_shape(100)                       # calibration for 100 tips
trees <- sim_tree_target(100, gamma = -2, colless = 1, nsim = 50, tol = 0.25,
                         calibration = cal)

# a 3 x 3 grid of tree shapes and the parameters of each cell
grid <- shape_grid(100, gamma = c(-2, -1, 0), colless = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                   calibration = cal)

See vignette("treeshapesim") for a walk-through. Many other tree statistics can be computed with treestats.

References

Aldous, D. (1996). Probability distributions on cladograms. In D. Aldous & R. Pemantle (Eds.), Random discrete structures (pp. 1–18). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-0719-1_1

Pybus, O. G., & Harvey, P. H. (2000). Testing macro-evolutionary models using incomplete molecular phylogenies. Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 267, 2267–2272. https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2000.1278
